defs.def: very correct and suitable for official or important occasions 穿着、言语、行为等
official; following an agreed or official way of doing things 正式的；合乎规矩的

ex.s: Tanya is also looking beyond special-occasion dresses to less formal clothing, ___63___ she plans to package as capsule wardrobes and offer to travellers, such as those headed to weddings abroad, with a longer-term rental period.
ex.t: Tanya也在超越特殊场合的连衣裙，转向更不正式的服装，____63____她计划打包成胶囊衣橱，提供给前往国外参加婚礼等、租期更长的旅客。

ex.s: As it turns out, however, this same concept-one that most consumers make many times each day with reflecting on it-is the basis of the more formal budget line concept in economics , which is explained below.
ex.t: 然而，事实证明，同一个概念——大多数消费者每天都会做出许多次、却不去反思的概念——是经济学中更正式的预算线概念的基础，下文将作解释。

ex.s: One of the most common mistakes in communication is trying to do too much. ___36___ There’s no value in delivering any kind of communication, whether written, spoken, formal, or informal, if the message doesn’t come across clearly.
ex.t: 沟通中最常见的错误之一就是试图做太多。___36___传递任何形式的沟通——无论是书面的、口头的、正式的还是非正式的——如果信息不能被清楚地理解，就没有价值。

ex.s: A formal invitation letter may use either the third person or first person “we” with the place and date often spelt out The wording and tone should be formal rather than conversational.
ex.t: 正式邀请函可以使用第三人称或第一人称"我们"，地点和日期通常要完整拼写出来。措辞和语气应该是正式的，而不是随意的。
